Now I see the changes more clearly:
Previous frame → Current frame:
- White diamond (W, 12px) at (6,17) → White object (W, 10px) at (12, 24) - moved to where orange square was!
- Orange square (O, 20px) at (12,24) → Orange square (O, 20px) at (14, 27) - moved further along trail
- Light gray objects (w, 8px) at (10,40) and (11,32) → DISAPPEARED
- Dark gray diamonds stayed at same positions
So clicking the orange square caused:
1. The white diamond (ahead of it) moved to where the orange square was
2. The orange square moved one step further along the trail
3. The light gray trail markers disappeared
This is similar to level 1! Clicking an object causes the chain to shift. The object ahead moves to the clicked position, and the clicked object moves forward.
Current top chain:
- White diamond at (12, 24) 
- Orange square at (14, 27)
- Dark gray diamond at (9, 49)
The chain order was: white → orange → dark gray
After clicking orange: white moved to orange's spot, orange moved forward
New order: white → orange → dark gray (same order but shifted)
Wait, but in level 1, clicking objects reversed the order. Let me think again...
In level 1:
- Original: white (closest to circle) → purple → dark gray (farthest)
- After clicking purple: white moved to purple's spot, purple moved back
- After clicking dark gray: dark gray moved to white's spot, white moved to dark gray's spot
- Final: dark gray (closest) → purple → white (farthest) - REVERSED
So the mechanic is: clicking an object causes it to swap with the object closest to the target.
In level 2, the "target" for the top chain might be the purple circle. Let me think about the chain order:
- Top chain: white diamond → orange square → dark gray diamond
- The dark gray diamond at (9, 49) is closest to the purple circle at ~ (18, 57)
- So the order from target is: dark gray → orange → white
If I want to reverse this, I need to click the orange square (which I did), then click the white diamond.
But wait, after clicking the orange square:
- White moved from (6,17) to (12,24)
- Orange moved from (12,24) to (14,27)
- Dark gray stayed at (9,49)
So now the order from the purple circle target is:
- Dark gray at (9,49) - closest
- Orange at (14,27) - middle
- White at (12,24) - farthest
Hmm, that doesn't seem right. The white diamond moved closer to the target, not farther. Let me reconsider.
Actually, looking at the trail in the image, the trail goes from white diamond → orange square → dark gray diamond. The dark gray diamond is closest to the purple circle. So the "front" of the chain is the dark gray diamond.
When I clicked the orange square (middle object), the white diamond (behind it) moved to where orange was, and orange moved forward toward the dark gray. This is like a shift forward.
So the mechanic might be: clicking an object causes everything behind it to shift forward by one position.
To reverse the order, I might need to click the farthest object (white diamond) to bring it to the front.
Let me try clicking the white diamond at (12, 24) now.
